title: OpenAI 下调估值目标至 1.25 万亿美元，拟融资至多 300 亿美元
content:
OpenAI 下调估值目标至 1.25 万亿美元，拟融资至多 300 亿美元
OpenAI lowers valuation target, raises up to $30 billion
OpenAI 接近完成至多 300 亿美元的新一轮融资，但将估值目标从最初的 1.4 万亿美元下调至 1.25 万亿美元。
原文汇总 FT 与 CNBC 报道，给出估值目标下调幅度、领投方和 IPO 时间线，便于追踪 OpenAI 融资进展。
2026年10月23日
OpenAI 即将完成一轮最高 300 亿美元的新融资，但为此下调了估值目标。据《金融时报》获得的内部文件，该公司最初向投资者提出的估值为 1.4 万亿美元。据CNBC 报道，这一数字此后已降至 1.25 万亿美元。《金融时报》称，需求弱于前几轮，一些投资方在早前融资中投入重金后出现“消化不良”。
阿联酋投资者和投资公司 Coatue 领投这轮 300 亿美元融资。此次融资被定位为潜在 IPO 之前的过渡。据 CNBC 报道，OpenAI 还在洽谈一项商业协议，以通过阿联酋获得额外的算力。
OpenAI 于 6 月向美国证券交易委员会（SEC）秘密提交了 IPO 招股说明书。首席财务官 Sarah Friar 在 8 月对员工表示，OpenAI 将在 2027 年前成为上市公司。首席执行官 Sam Altman 在 9 月表示，时机不利于上市。他早在 6 月就已在内部传达了这一点。竞争对手 Anthropic 也在筹备 IPO，目标估值在 1.5 万亿至 2 万亿美元之间。

report.summary: OpenAI is finalizing a funding round of up to $30 billion at a trimmed $1.25 trillion valuation, down from $1.4 trillion, as a bridge ahead of a planned IPO.
report.background: OpenAI has spent two years converting venture-scale money into what looks like infrastructure finance. Frontier training runs, inference for hundreds of millions of users, and datacenter build-outs have turned capital raising into a recurring event rather than a milestone. That has pulled in sovereign wealth funds — the UAE prominent among them — alongside crossover investors like Coatue, whose cheque sizes dwarf traditional VC rounds. The logic is circular but real: more compute buys better models, better models buy revenue, revenue justifies valuation. The catch is that each successive round needs fresh buyers. Reports that demand was weaker than in prior rounds, with some backers suffering 'digestion' after heavy earlier commitments, suggests the pool of price-insensitive capital is thinning. Meanwhile Anthropic is preparing its own listing at a reported $1.5–2 trillion target, so the IPO window is contested. OpenAI confidentially filed with the SEC in June, and CFO Sarah Friar has pointed to 2027 for going public, while Sam Altman has publicly questioned market timing.
key_points: Valuation cut by roughly $150 billion: internal documents first floated $1.4 trillion, and CNBC reports the figure has since settled at $1.25 trillion. The direction of travel matters more than the absolute number — it is the first visible markdown in OpenAI's private valuation trajectory, and it was made to get the round closed rather than after a failed close.

Up to $30 billion is being raised, led by UAE investors and Coatue. The size keeps OpenAI in the largest private financings ever recorded, but the structure — sovereign capital plus a single US crossover fund — concentrates the cap table and gives Gulf backers unusual leverage over the company's direction.

Demand was softer than in prior rounds. The FT cites investor 'indigestion' among backers who already deployed heavily in earlier OpenAI rounds, implying portfolio concentration limits are now a real constraint on how fast the company can raise.

The raise is explicitly framed as a bridge to IPO, not a destination. OpenAI confidentially filed its S-8 paperwork in June and the CFO has targeted 2027 for listing, though Altman has said publicly that the timing is unfavourable.

A parallel commercial deal would give OpenAI additional compute through the UAE, tying the financing to the resource the money is meant to buy. That bundling of capital and compute is becoming the standard shape of frontier AI deals.

The competitive clock is ticking: Anthropic is also preparing a listing, reportedly targeting a $1.5–2 trillion valuation, meaning OpenAI may not be the first or the most generously priced AI IPO to market.
report.impact: For the AI industry, a down round in all but name is a signal that private markets are starting to price AI companies against something other than momentum. Sovereign funds are replacing VCs as the marginal buyer, which shifts governance and geographies of compute toward the Gulf. For developers, the practical consequence is that capital discipline usually arrives as pricing discipline: expect more aggressive API tiering, usage-based enterprise contracts, and pressure to convert free users rather than subsidise them. Anyone building on proprietary APIs should reduce single-vendor exposure and keep model-swapping abstractions in place. For regular users, the era of heavily subsidised frontier access is unlikely to reverse immediately, but cheaper tiers will increasingly be gated by capability or rate limits, and the pace of free-tier upgrades may slow as the company optimises toward the numbers an IPO prospectus demands.
report.tools: To follow the story: SEC EDGAR full-text search for the confidential filing and eventual S-1, Crunchbase or PitchBook for cap-table and round tracking, and The Decoder's newsletter for reporting summaries. If you want insurance against API pricing shifts, keep a portable stack — LiteLLM or OpenRouter for model routing, Ollama plus an open-weights model such as Llama or Qwen for local fallback, and vLLM if you self-host.
